narrative.overview: Attyx's surface is a dark control panel for someone driving machines — and increasingly, driving agents. The whole system is built on schematic discipline: a near-black ground, an ambient engineering grid, corner coordinates, numbered parts, hairline dividers, and a single typeface that never breaks character. It reads like the precise technical drawing of an instrument, not a marketing page about one. The product tracks AI agent lifecycle, drives panes over IPC, and exposes a CLI for orchestration — so the site should feel like the console an operator watches those agents from: exact, legible, alive only where state changes. The palette is Phosphor & Graphite — white-as-phosphor signal glowing against a graphite-to-carbon ramp. White is the only color; everything else is a degree of grey falling toward true black.
keyCharacteristics: True-black ground (#0a0a0a) with a single phosphor ink (#f0f0f0).
One typeface — Space Mono — across display, body, and code. No pairing.
Schematic motifs: ambient grid, corner coordinates, numbered features, hairline rules.
Flat by default; one dramatic shadow lifts the product screenshot off the page.
Quiet at rest, tactile on interaction — hover inverts, reveals a line, fills white.
Agent-aware framing: the console watches and drives; restraint is the operator's calm.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Phosphor White is the only color that carries meaning. Emphasis comes from weight, size, or contrast against graphite — never from introducing a hue.

rules.name: The Quotation Rule
rules.body: Chromatic color (amber, traffic lights) is permitted only when it quotes a real interface element the user already recognizes. Decorative color is forbidden.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Space Mono everywhere, no exceptions. The monospace is the brand; a sans body would make Attyx look like everything else.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Anything functioning as a label, coordinate, or status readout takes 0.2em tracking and usually uppercase. Body copy stays at normal tracking so it never reads as chrome.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are coplanar and separated by hairlines. A drop shadow anywhere except the hero screenshot is a bug. If a card needs a shadow to read, fix the border or tonal step.

dos: Do keep True Black (#0a0a0a) as the ground and Phosphor White (#f0f0f0) as the only accent.
Do set everything in Space Mono — display, body, code, labels. One voice.
Do give labels, coordinates, and status readouts 0.2em tracking, usually uppercase.
Do keep surfaces flat and separated by hairline borders; reserve the one deep shadow for the product screenshot.
Do make the payoff the state change — invert the primary button, draw the feature-cell hairline, fill on hover.
Do earn every motif; if it's purely decorative, cut it.
Do lean the positioning into agent workflows — agent-status tracking, IPC orchestration, the attyx CLI.
Do verify body text hits WCAG AA (>=4.5:1); Ash (#606060) and Smoke (#808080) on #0a0a0a are close — bump toward the ink end for small or long text.
donts: Don't introduce a second brand hue. Chromatic color is allowed only as a quotation (amber star, traffic lights).
Don't use gradient text or background-clip: text.
Don't drift toward warm cream / parchment / editorial near-white palettes — the 2026 AI default.
Don't tip into neon-green-on-black hacker cosplay, matrix rain, or heavy CRT scanlines.
Don't add SaaS gradient heroes, hero-metric templates, identical floating card grids, or enterprise chrome.
Don't pair Space Mono with a clean sans for readability. The monospace is the brand.
Don't add drop shadows to cards or panels; fix the border or tonal step instead.
Don't ship animations without a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce alternative (boot sequence, hero stagger, feature hovers currently lack one).
